decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style=""><span style="text-indent: -18pt;">The proposal fails to provide a sufficient number of car parking spaces within the curtilage of the site and furthermore their size are insufficient to accommodate a standard
vehicle, rendering them unusable for their intended purpose. The proposal&nbsp;</span><span style="text-indent: -24px;">would fail to provide a sufficient level of parking to meet the needs of future occupiers</span><span style="text-indent: -18pt;">, resulting in an increase in the demand for on-street parking, to the detriment
of highway safety and the free flow of traffic. The proposal is therefore
contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy CS1 of the
Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policies DM1, DM26 and DM43 of the Harrow Development
Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and Policy T6.1 of the London Plan
(2021).</span></p><p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-indent:-18.0pt;mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The living/kitchen area within proposed Flat 2
would have only one opening providing its only source of light
and outlook, which would directly face the proposed boundary fence adjacent to
Flats 1 and 2. The light and outlook to this habitable room would
therefore be inadequate for future occupiers and would result in a
perception of a loss of privacy between Flat 2 and the private
amenity space for Flat 1. &nbsp;The proposal therefore fails to provide a high
standard of residential accommodation for future occupiers and is therefore contrary to the
high-quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework
(2024), Policy D3(D7) and D6 of The London Plan (2021) and Policies DM1 and
DM26 of the Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the
Residential Design Guide SPD (2010).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The proposal, by reason of the fragmented and
contrived subdivision of the rear garden, would fail to provide a practical, or
high-quality arrangement of private amenity space for future occupiers and results in a refuse area which is inconvenient for future occupiers due to its siting and convoluted access.&nbsp; As such, the development is contrary to the National
Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3(D7), D3(D10) and D6 of the London
Plan (2021), Policies DM1, DM26 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management
Policies Local Plan (2013), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the
Housing Design Standards LPG (2023).</p>
description: Conversion of dwelling into three flats (2 X 2 bed & 1 X 3 bed); Single and two storey side extension; Single and two storey rear extension; Alterations and extension to roof to raise ridge height and form rear dormers; Roof lights in front and side roof slopes; External alterations, Private amenity space; Boundary treatment; Bin and cycle stores, Landscaping, Parking to front (Demolition of attached garage and outbuildings at rear)
